question: Root cause found: no literal page reload exists — the 'auto-refresh' is two existing full-screen re-render swaps (AuthGuard's spinner, then Home's categoriesReady gate), and the category mismatch is DEFAULT_CATEGORIES (a hardcoded 24-item fallback) being unconditionally replaced by the live list on every load, worsened by the backend re-minting its Sheets auth client on every request. Fix: cache the last-fetched live category list client-side (same pattern as entity 058's LAST_CATEGORY_KEY) so a returning device's first paint already matches reality, and memoize the backend auth client so warm instances stop paying a redundant token mint. Is this approach and the 9 ACs (6 offline, 3 interactive) sound and ready to move to build?

artifacts.summary: Spec resolves all four ideation open questions with code-level evidence (file:line citations, no speculation): Save is correctly gated on a live category being selected (entity 058, not a bug); there is no reload mechanism in the code at all; the perceived swap is two legitimate full-screen re-renders (auth spinner, then categories-loading state); and categories visibly change because DEFAULT_CATEGORIES (a hardcoded 24-item build-time fallback) always gets replaced by the live Sheet-backed list, with disjoint id schemes so no tile survives the swap. Fix caches the live list client-side (localStorage, mirroring 058's existing pattern) so a returning device's first paint already matches reality, plus memoizes the backend's Sheets auth client to cut redundant per-request overhead on warm instances. 9 ACs (AC-1-8 offline via mocked mounts, AC-9 interactive live drive), +100 LOC/4-5 files at +-30% tolerance, cold-start elimination itself explicitly out of scope as a captain cost decision.
